elsewhere: 3 parts: The ending, After combat, Combat

comments.text: SQRPACI01, the battlefield's figure tables, with the code COMBAT needs for backstabs and timed effects after them. This table is each figure's height, which COM.PREP sets for the area (set_tile_figures): in a 3D area, as here, 0 for figure 0, open ground, and $0A for figures 1 to 26; outdoors $0A only for figures 1 to 11, 21 and 22. Nothing steps onto a figure with a height (move, try_step), and a line of sight passes one only above it (sight). The rest of each 128-byte table, here and in the three that follow, is left from the file's making.
figure_height for figures 64 to 127, left from the file's making like those from 27.
Each figure's ground height, added to a combatant's own height for its eyes (heights): 0 for figures 0 to 11.
figure_ground for figures 64 to 127, left from the file's making like those from 12.
How much each figure blocks a line of sight that meets it below its height, taken from the line's allowance (sight): 0 for figure 0, 5 for figures 1 to 10.
figure_opacity for figures 64 to 127, left from the file's making like those from 11.
The tile each figure is drawn with: figure n is tile $30 + n. Tiles 0 to $2F are the combatants' icons.
figure_tiles for figures 64 to 127: tiles $70 to $AF, past the 48 + 7 tiles the battle has.
The tiles' graphics, $91B0: 18 bytes a tile, nine characters then nine colours, so tile $30 (figure 0) is at $9510.
The tiles' high byte.
The map, $8C00: a byte a square, row by row, last_column + 1 to a row. Bit 7 is set while someone stands there; bits 0-6 are the figure.
The map's high byte.
The entry list, $8B00: four bytes an entry, across, down, its tile and its pose (bit 7 hiding it); $FF,$FF across and down for one off the map.
The entry list's high byte.
How many entries each group has: one group of 64 here.
How many groups: 1.
The tile for a square where two groups' entries stand (who_tile): 0.
Each group's tile for a square two of its entries share: 0.
The view's last left column, 49, and top row, 19 ($0611): the map less the 7-square view.
The view's last top row.
The map's last column, 55 (56 across), and row, 25 ($0613: 26 down).
The map's last row; the five bytes after it are not used.
1: a line of sight must be clear both ways (sight).
The view's size in squares: 7.
How far centre_view puts the view's corner from the square it centres on: 3. The bytes after it, to $067F, are left from the file's making.
Left from the file's making, up to the code at $0680.

Before an attack: $2B7C = 0, then for one that can backstab (can_backstab) attacking a target from behind, the multiplier into $2B7C. From behind means the attack's direction ($033D) is the opposite of the first attack made on the target since its own turn ($A500, from note_attack): the target is taken to face whoever attacked it first, so a thief cannot backstab a target nobody else is fighting.

Carry set when the combatant can backstab: it has a thief level ($6BCB), which gives the multiplier in $B0, (level - 1) / 4 + 2, so 2 at levels 1 to 4, 3 at 5 to 8; its armour, if any is readied ($6DEC), is item type $32; and its readied weapon, if any (weapon_loaded), is of type $07, $08 or $22 to $25.
Multiplies the damage ($A4F7) by $2B7C when there is a multiplier.

The undead the combatant can see that has the lowest type ($6BA3, 0 for one that is not undead) and has not been turned ($A680 bit 7): its entry in A and $2B76, its type in $2B75; $80 in both when there is none. Through enemies_seen within 128 squares and into_targets; the combatant is loaded again after.

Runs event X for entry A ($2B22): event X's list of timed-effect kinds is found in $DB7A, under the I/O area (lists ending in 0, list 0 empty), and for each kind in it the entry is loaded (load_combatant) and run_effect runs with Y = 0.
Event X for the combatant in hand ($A4F4), which is then loaded again.
Event X for the target ($A4F5), which is then loaded again (load_target).

Timed effect kind A for the loaded combatant, Y its argument ($2B23). When the combatant holds an effect of that kind (has_effect) the effect's routine runs: its address from $DA63 (low) and $DAEE (high) by kind is written into the JSR at $07A8, the spell file the low bits of $DC13 + kind name is loaded into slot 7 (load_spell_file), and the routine is called with A = $2B23; then copy_parts. For the area kinds (area_kinds) an effect held by anyone counts too: each entry from 63 down ($2B02) that holds one, when the combatant is within 2 squares that a line from it reaches (list_from_point).
The effect routine's address, low byte, written into this JSR.
The effect routine's address, high byte. After the call, copy_parts.
The three timed-effect kinds that reach everyone within 2 squares of whoever holds them: $15, $2D and $2E.
The sprite position of the view's top left square: 32 across, 58 down (missile_leg).

Ends timed effect X: its kind into $6E6E and the entry emptied ($4900 = 0). When its fourth byte ($4B80) has bit 7 set, the kind's routine runs again with that byte as its argument (run_effect's call), to undo the effect. Then slot 7's file back (reload_slot7).
Left from the file's making: the tail of a JMP $9B40, then an RTS.

The picture of a missile from item type Y flying in direction $033D, into sprite 6 ($E2C0): picture $13 for types $57 and up and for $2F, one picture whatever the direction. Other types have three pictures, one for up and down, one for the diagonals and one across (direction_pictures): $10 to $12 for types $55 and $56, $14 and those below 8, $0D to $0F for the rest. The colour pair's number goes in $2B1E: 8, 7, 6, 5 or 4 in that order. The picture is loaded (load_missile_picture) and then copied over itself mirrored for the direction (missile_byte_mirror, missile_byte_place).
For each direction 0-7, which of a missile's three pictures it shows: 0 up and down, 1 diagonal, 2 across.
1 for the directions whose picture is mirrored left to right: 5, 6 and 7, the westward ones.
1 for the directions whose picture is turned upside down: 3, 4 and 5, the southward ones.
A line's ends: the combatant in hand's square into $0348/$034A (line_start) and the target's ($A4F5) into $0349/$034B, each when there is one.

A missile from the combatant in hand to its target: sound 1, a pause (pause_90) and the line's ends (both_squares). From $6586, where the spell files come in with the ends set, sprite 6 flies a leg at a time: the view centred on the leg's start (centre_view), the part of the line in view (missile_leg), the speed (missile_speed) and the flight (missile_flight). When the line runs out of the view a second leg follows with the view centred on the target's square.
Sprite 6's step on each axis: the pixel distances to its end (missile_gap), doubled together until one reaches 128, into $0354 and $0355.
Carry clear when square X across, Y down is in the 7 by 7 view.

Flies sprite 6, alone on the screen ($D015 = $40), from where missile_leg put it to $0378/$0379: each step adds missile_speed's figures to two fractions ($C3, $C4) and moves the sprite a pixel on each axis that carries, west and north when $28 and $29 say. With $2B1A not 0 the sprite's colour changes every step, and with it positive the picture too (next_missile_picture), with no wait; otherwise each step waits a little (missile_wait). Sprites off at the end.
A short wait: delay from $2E23 with X = 2 and $B1 = 0. $6635 takes X as it is.
The pixel distances from sprite 6 to its end ($0378/$0379), without their signs, into $0354/$0355.

The leg of a missile's flight that is in the view: the line from the shooter to the target (line_between, up to 128 squares), its first square in view (the start itself when it is) and its last, each as a sprite position, 24 x (square less the view's corner) + square_origin. Sprite 6 goes to the first and the last goes into $0378/$0379. $2B4A = 1 when the last is not the target's square, so another leg follows.
The computer has nothing to attack: with no missile weapon readied (range $6D9D 0, find_readied) the combatant guards; otherwise its turn ends.

A target for the computer within A squares ($0364): carry clear when there is one, faced (face_target). The target it remembers ($A600) is kept, unless this turn's choice was the computer's ($2B20 bit 7), while it is still there and event 1 lets it be targeted (pick_target). Otherwise it is forgotten and up to ten random picks are made among the enemies the combatant can see (enemies_seen, into_targets), each refused one crossed off the list; the first that event 1 allows is remembered. When none is found and the sight allowance ($034E) was 0, the search is made again with it at $FF, which lets a line pass about fifty walls: the computer goes for an enemy it cannot see. Carry set with none. Slot 7's file back, and $034E 0.

The computer's turn for the combatant in hand. A key or the joystick takes the party back from QUICK first (ai_key) and the menu bar is cleared; one no longer able (able_side) ends its turn, and one back under the player's control ($6C0C bit 7 clear) gets initiative 20 (initiative_20) so its turn comes round again at once, for the player. The tries are shuffled (ai_shuffle), the panel shown and the message pause run; then one that gives up (morale), is out of the fight ($6C00 bit 7) or uses an item (ai_use_item) ends its turn. Its guard stops. A spell begun in an earlier turn is cast now (cast_spell, $2B20 bit 7 set) and ends the turn; one that was lost ($A440 = $80) goes straight to the weapon; otherwise it may turn undead (ai_turn_undead, which ends the turn) or cast (ai_cast, which returns). Then the weapon (ai_pick_weapon) and a target within 128 squares (ai_target), with none ai_wait. Event 14 runs for it; one with no initiative left ends its turn. Then the loop at $67F2. One fleeing ($2B70) moves. One that can shoot (can_shoot, range $6D9D 2 or more) attacks its remembered target when it can see it within the range; otherwise a random enemy one of its squares can see, within the range, or within 2 squares for one that cannot shoot (enemies_seen_any), becomes the target, a shooter whose nearest enemy is within a square choosing its weapon again. With no enemy in sight it moves. An attack is a sweep when it can sweep (ai_sweep); otherwise it faces the target and notes the attack, and a shot at 2 squares or more is a long shot ($2B42) with its ammunition counted (can_strike with A = 1, monster_ammo). After the attack, with attacks left, round the loop again, choosing a target afresh. A move ($6884): the moves left shown; a pure magic-user (class mask $6BEB = 1) that is not fleeing stays where it is (movement 0); with under 2 half squares of movement left, ai_wait. The heading ($2B3C) is towards the target, or for one fleeing away from the other side: the party's 3D facing ($49C2) x 2, turned round for side 0. Up to four tries at a step (ai_try_dir, try_turns); a step taken draws the ready pose (ready_pose), gives a fleeing one's enemies their swings (ai_leave) and makes the step (take_step), then back round the loop. One fleeing that the map's edge stops on its first try flees the battle (flee); when every try fails its movement goes to 0 and it stops fleeing.
Carry clear when a weapon is readied (weapon_loaded) and the computer did not choose to fight hand to hand ($2B5E = 0).

Whether the combatant in hand can step in direction A ($033D), carry clear when it can: every one of its squares (my_square_fb, next_square) must step onto the map (step; $6DD5 = $B0, set when one would leave it), onto a figure with no height (figure_height) and onto no other combatant (who_is_at, only_self_at), and its movement ($A540) must cover the step's cost (step_cost at $7AD0). The combatant ($2B43) is put back in hand.

$2B7B for a long shot ($2B42): -2 when the distance ($034F) is beyond a third of the range less 1 (($0364 - 1) / 3), -5 beyond twice that; otherwise 0. attack_routine adds it to the AC figure, which makes a long shot easier to hit rather than harder. A player's shot comes with $0364 as AIM left it, 128, not the weapon's range.
For a westward direction (flip_across), the picture byte's four pixel pairs reversed (mirror_pairs). Y is kept in $03E0, the byte in $03DE.

Where picture byte Y goes in the mirrored copy, into X, with the byte in A. Upside down (flip_down) its place is 62 less Y, with down_shifts putting each row's three bytes back in order; mirrored left to right (flip_across) the three bytes of each row change places (across_shifts). $B1 counts the byte's place, 0-2, as Y goes down. Both at once, 62 less Y alone turns the picture half round.
How far a byte moves in its row to mirror the picture left to right: -2, 0, +2.
The same for a picture turned upside down, whose rows are already reversed: +2, 0, -2.

1 when direction $033D is one of those round the move's direction $A4E5 (away_masks): the three nearest a straight move, the five nearest a diagonal one; free_swings asks it which enemies a move leads away from.
move_away's shift: bit $033D of the mask into bit 0.
For each direction 0-7, the directions round it as bits: 0, 1 and 7 for 0 (north), 0 to 3 and 7 for 1, and on.
Back to the head entry (take_combatant while $6C01 has bit 7), then carry set when the combatant has not swung during this move ($A480 bit 0, which it then sets); carry clear when it has.
The combatant in hand remembers the target ($A4F5) in $A600; $6A28 remembers A.
remember_target for A.
The combatant in hand's initiative ($A380) = 20: it acts next. $6A31 sets A.
The combatant in hand's initiative = A.
A = the combatant in hand's movement left, in half squares ($A540).
The combatant in hand's movement = 0; $6A41 sets A.
The combatant in hand's movement = A.
Missile picture A with the colour pair $DCE1 + A gives it ($2B1E), into sprite 6 (load_missile_picture).

Missile picture A ($2B1D), one of 20 at $DD00 (64 bytes each, under the I/O area), into sprite 6's image at $E2C0, X into $2B1A for missile_flight. Colour pair $2B1E: its first byte ($DCEE + 2 x pair) to sprite 6's colour and to the multicolour switches ($D01C), its second ($DCEF) to the two shared colours, low nibble $D025 and high nibble $D026. Sprite 6's pointer ($CFFE) = $8B.
The next of missile pictures 6 to 9 twice over (after 9, 6), each loaded (missile_pictures). Returns N set.

The list of what is seen ($9800, its count first) into the target list ($A640, count $2B13), each entry as a target (seen_target); an entry listed twice is crossed off ($FF, drop_target). The target ($A4F5) is put back; A = the count.

The caster's panel (show_combatant), CASTS A SPELL (message $27) under its name, then SPELL: (COMBAT message 10) on the bottom row with the spell's name ($2B41) after it, and the message pause. ECL64 is the combat's spell code, loaded where a block's script goes in the adventure.
Casts spell $2B41: the caster's level (caster_level), the announcement (announce_spell), then load_and_cast.

The spell's record (load_spell_record, which also loads SPELLE00 at $A700), $2B09 and $A4FC cleared, SPELLE00's two steps (spell_targets, spell_flight), timed effect $19 on the caster ended (end_effect_19), then a jump to the spell's own routine ($2B39/$2B3A): one in SPELLE00, or spell_area ($29F7).
SPELLE00, file 0, into slot 7 at $A700 (load_slot7), then spell $2B41's nine-byte record, $D81B + 9 x (spell - 1) under the I/O area, into spell_record ($2B32-$2B3A).
The caster's level for spell $2B41 into $2B05: the cleric level ($6BCA) when bit 7 of the spell's flags is set (spell_bits), otherwise the magic-user level ($6BC9).

The target's saving throw against the spell, into $2AFE, bit 7 set when it fails. A spell whose save byte ($2B36) is 0 allows none: it fails. Otherwise the target needs its save of the kind in bits 2-4 ($6B9A + kind) on a d20: 20 always saves and 1 always fails. Bits 5-7 change it: 5 to 7 make the save needed 1 to 3 higher; 1 to 4 add that much and the target's $6DA7 (its readied items' byte 5) to the roll. Event 12 for the target may change the roll. Slot 7's file back after.

The spell's timed effect on the target: kind $2B37, none when 0. Event 9 for the target may take it away; it lands only when the save failed ($2AFE bit 7) and a touch spell hits (touch_hit), otherwise IS UNAFFECTED (message $0C). Its time ($2AFB) is the time per level ($2B34) x the caster's level + the base ($2B33 low six bits). An effect of the same kind already on the target is kept, and nothing added, when it lasts for ever (time 0) or longer than the new one, unless the new one lasts for ever; otherwise it ends (end_effect) and the new one goes into a free entry (free_effect): kind, target, time and $2B09 in $4900, $4940, $4980 and $4B80; the spell files come in at $9A0D with the kind and time set. Then spell_landed, and slot 7's file back.
For the spell files: spell_effect from the point where the kind ($2AFD) and the time ($2AFB) are set: an older effect of that kind is kept or replaced, then the new one added.
Not used: 0, $40, $80 and $C0.
Finds an empty timed-effect entry (find_entry_x for kind 0, any holder): carry set with it in X.
For the spell files: spell_damage with the save marked failed ($2AFE = $80), so the damage is whole.

The spell's damage on the target: the damage the spell file set ($2B00; nothing when 0) into $A4F7, then event 6 for the target. A save ($2AFE bit 7 clear) halves it, or for a spell whose save bits 0-1 are 1 takes it all. A touch spell must hit (touch_hit); a miss is reported as an attack (report_attack). Damage left: sound 6, the panel (show_panel, status_window), the sparkle (X = 0), apply_damage, then IS HIT FOR (message $0F) n POINTS OF DAMAGE and its kind from the lowest bit set in $2AFF (FROM FIRE to FROM ACID, messages $1B-$1F), and report_result. Sprites off and slot 7's file back.

For the spell files: puts kind A ($2AFD) on the working character, in the first empty one of its ten bytes at $6BAD (the list has_item_type reads) unless it is there already, and stores the character (store_character). With all ten full it becomes a timed effect that lasts for ever ($2AFB = 0, $2B09 = $7F) on the party position in hand, through spell_effect from $9A0D.

For the spell files: takes kind A off the working character: out of its list at $6BAD when it is there, otherwise the timed effect of that kind on it ends (find_entry, end_effect). The character is stored.
Two bits of spell X's flags ($DC13 + spell, under the I/O area): the flags shifted right Y times, AND 3.
The spell file numbered by spell_bits (X, Y) into slot 7.
Loads file A into slot 7 (load_resource_a, X = 7: SPELLEnn at $A700), sprites off meanwhile and back as they were.
Loads file $2B15 into slot 7 again when its bit 7 is set (keep_slot7).
For the spell files: the file in slot 7 ($6E1A) is to come back after (reload_slot7): it goes in $2B15 with bit 7 set.
For the spell files: $2B15 = 0, nothing to load back.
For the spell files: the spell's damage ($2B00) = A dice of 10 sides (roll_dice), A kept in $2B0E; carry clear. $9B5C rolls d8s, $9B60 d6s, $9B64 d4s.
A dice of 8 sides into $2B00.
A dice of 6 sides into $2B00.
A dice of 4 sides into $2B00.
For the spell files: X = the number of targets ($2B13); with none, a return from the spell file's routine as well.
For the spell files: crosses spell_area's current target ($2B06) off the list (drop_target).
Crosses target X off the list ($A640 + X = $FF).
For the spell files: the combatant in hand loaded (load_current) and its readied weapon found (weapon_loaded), then the target loaded again (load_target); A = the weapon's slot, N set for none.
Event 18 for movement ($2B0D = 1) rather than attacks; $9B92 takes A, the value, for attacks.
Event 18 for the party position in hand ($6DB4): A, the number it may change, kept in $2B19 and returned.
Spell X's byte at $DC9F (under the I/O area): its priority for the computer and flags (ai_cast).
For a touch spell (range $FF): a hit roll as for a weapon (target_ac, hit_roll) on the target, A = $A4FB, 1 for a hit and 0 for a miss; any other spell returns with Z clear, as for a hit.
The spell's range in squares from its record ($2B32; $FF counts as 0): the high nibble x the caster's level ($2B05) / 4, plus the low nibble, plus 1.

SPELLE65, the combat graphics and spell tables, as COM.PREP loaded them: 30 characters here (240 bytes, to $D200), tiles 1 to 7 from $A7F8 (to $9522), the two pictures for a fallen body from $A876 (to $E200), and from $A8F6 the spell tables and missile pictures (to $D800-$E1FF). By the time a spell is cast SPELLE00, the spell code, has been loaded over them, and load_and_cast calls it here: $A700 finds the spell's targets by the low nibble of the record's fourth byte ($2B35): 0 the caster itself, $0F one the caster aims at, 8 and up everyone within (nibble AND 7) squares of the point aimed at (spell_targets_at).
SPELLE65's tiles 1 to 7 for the battlefield's figures, 18 bytes each (nine characters, nine colours), which COM.PREP copies to $9522.

In SPELLE00: sound 3 and a pause, then, when the spell is aimed at a square other than the caster's, a missile (missile picture 6) flies from the caster to it (fly_missile from $6586), for most kinds of targeting. In this snapshot the bytes are SPELLE65's.
SPELLE65's two sprite pictures for a fallen body, red and black, which COM.PREP copies to $E200 (pictures $88 and $89, lie_down).

SPELLE65's $A00 bytes that COM.PREP copies to $D800, under the I/O area: from $D81B the spell records (nine bytes a spell, load_spell_record), the effect routines' addresses at $DA63 and $DAEE, the events' lists of effect kinds at $DB7A, the spell flags at $DC13 (spell_bits), the computer's spell information at $DC9F (spell_info), the missile colours at $DCE1 and $DCEE, and from $DD00 the twenty missile pictures (load_missile_picture). Its first 27 bytes ($D800-$D81A) are written over after the copy.
The spell records, nine bytes a spell from spell 1, bound for $D81B.
The timed-effect routines' addresses, low bytes by kind, bound for $DA63.
The same, high bytes, bound for $DAEE.
The events' lists of timed-effect kinds, each ending in 0, bound for $DB7A.
The spell flags by spell (and by effect kind, for the file that holds each kind's routine), bound for $DC13.
The computer's information on each spell, bound for $DC9F.
Each missile picture's colour pair, bound for $DCE1, and the pairs themselves from $ADE4 ($DCEE).
The missile pictures, 64 bytes each, which land at $DD00: four and a little of the twenty here, to $AEFF; the rest of the file lies under SPELLN00 from $AF00.
SPELLN00, the spell names and spell messages: each string's address, low bytes, by number (print_spell_name); the names are 1 to $38 and the messages $39 on (spell_message).
spell_name_lo for strings $40 to $7F: messages 7 to $3F, and past the last message bytes that point nowhere.
The strings' addresses, high bytes.
spell_name_hi for strings $40 to $7F.
The strings, each ending in 0: BLESS, CURSE, CURE LIGHT WOUNDS ... RESTORATION, then IS CHARMED ... SURRENDERS.
The spell messages from GAZES... (message $14) to SURRENDERS ($3F).

GDRIVE00, the battlefield's grid driver: a table of jumps the combat code calls, then the routines behind them. $C000 draws the view, the 7 by 7 squares from its corner ($037E across, $037F down) (redraw_view).

The view a row down, redrawn (view_down). Nothing in the combat modules or the spell files calls $C003 to $C00C; the view moves through follow_view and centre_view, which use the routines behind them.
The view a row up, redrawn (view_up).
The view a column right, redrawn (view_right).
The view a column left, redrawn (view_left).
Puts entry $9B of group $B1 on the map at square FB/FC (put_entry).
Takes entry $9B of group $B1 off the map (lift_entry).
Lists the entries standing on square FB/FC: their groups at $9700 and their numbers at $9780, the list ending in $FF (find_at).
Gives map square FB/FC figure $B1, keeping its occupied bit, and redraws it (write_figure).
Map square FB/FC's figure into $035F and A (read_figure).
Entry $9B of group $B1: its square into FB/FC, its pose (byte 3) set to $9C, and the square redrawn (show_at_entry).
Counts the other groups' entries round square FB/FC (neighbours). Nothing in the combat modules or the spell files calls it.
Redraws square FB/FC with the cursor, sprite 7, over it (draw_cursor).
Moves FB/FC a square in direction $033D; $B0 = 1, and FB/FC unchanged, when the step would leave the map (step_square).
Moves entry $9B a square in direction $033D, the view following it (move_one).
Whether entry $0344 can see entry $0345 (their groups in $0346 and $0347): $0353 = 0 when it can, the distance in $034F (sight_between).
Draws each square that entry $0344 can see (seen_from_entry). Nothing in the combat modules or the spell files calls it.
Whether square $0348/$034A can see square $0349/$034B, both at ground height (sight_plain). Nothing in the combat modules or the spell files calls it.
The squares of the line from $0348/$034A to $0349/$034B, into $9700 (across) and $9780 (down), how many in $034F (trace_between).
mark_seen from square $0348/$034A at ground height (seen_view_plain). Nothing in the combat modules or the spell files calls it.
The entries of group $0347 that entry $0344 can see, nearest first, into $9800 (how many in $9800, the entries from $9801) with their distances at $9880 (gather_seen).
Four spare entries, $C03F to $C048, and four more at $C051 to $C05A: each jumps to an RTS ($CB95-$CB9C).
Redraws square FB/FC without the cursor (draw_square).
Centres the view on square FB/FC, as far as the map's edges allow, and draws it (centre_on_square).
$4C/$4D = $AB times $4B (mul8). Nothing outside GDRIVE00 calls $C05D or $C060.
$4C/$4D divided by $AB: the quotient in $4B, the remainder in $4D (div8).
The address of entry $9B of group $B1 into $9E/$9F (entry_addr).
The tracing half of line_between, for a line already set up: its squares into $9700/$9780 (trace). The spell file SPELLE00 calls it.

Draws the squares from FB/FC, which shows at screen square $4E/$4F (counting from 1), across to screen column $0378 and down to row $0379; nothing while $036C is 0. Each square is a tile of 3 by 3 characters: a square with someone on it (map bit 7) shows the occupant's tile (who_tile) unless $033C is set or all there are hidden, an empty one its figure's tile (figure_tiles). The tile's nine characters and nine colours ($0600 + 18 x tile) go to the screen (page $0288, from row 3 x $4F - 2 and column 3 x $4E - 2) and colour RAM by square_offsets; with $033F set each character also moves the cursor over the square (cursor_sprite). FB/FC are put back at the end (back_square).
Not an entry: the colour loop at $C10C reads square_offsets as $C140 + 9 to 17, which is $C149 again.
Where a square's nine characters go, from its top left: three rows of three, 40 bytes apart.
Multiplies $AB by $4B: the product in $4C (low) and $4D and A (high). $AB is used up.

The tile for whoever stands on square FB/FC, in A and $B1, $FF for nobody. Over every group's entries ($0604, $060A groups of $0606 + group): an entry on the square that is not hidden (byte 3 bit 7; group $035B shows its hidden ones too) gives its group its tile (byte 2), or the group's crowd tile ($060C + group) when a second of the same group is there. One group there gives that tile; two or more give mixed_tile ($060B).
The view's top row ($037F) one down, no further than last_top ($0611), and redrawn; nothing when it is there already.
Draws the whole view: the 7 by 7 squares (view_size, into $0378/$0379) from the view's corner ($037E/$037F) at screen square 1,1, with FB/FC kept (keep_square).
The view's top row one up, not above row 0, and redrawn.
The view's left column one right, no further than last_left ($0610), and redrawn.
The view's left column one left, not past column 0, and redrawn.
$9E/$9F = the entry list ($0604/$0605) + 4 x (entry $9B plus the sizes of the groups before group $B1).

Puts entry $9B of group $B1 on square FB/FC, only when the entry is off the map (its square $FF,$FF) and the square is on it: the square into the entry, the map square's occupied bit (bit 7) set, and the square redrawn (draw_one).
Redraws square FB/FC when it is in the view: its place in the view (counting from 1) into $4E/$4F and $0378/$0379, so draw_squares draws that one square.

Takes entry $9B of group $B1 off the map: its square into FB/FC and the entry's square set to $FF,$FF; when nobody else stands there (find_at) the map square's occupied bit is cleared. The square is redrawn.
Fills $9700-$97FF with $FF: the lists of squares and entries start empty.
Lists every entry on square FB/FC, over all groups: the group at $9700 + n and the entry at $9780 + n, up to $80 of them, the rest left $FF (clear_found).
The address of map square FB/FC into $07/$08: the map ($0602/$0603) + FC x (last_column + 1) + FB.
Map square FB/FC's figure (bits 0-6) = $B1, its occupied bit kept; the square redrawn.
Map square FB/FC's figure, bits 0-6, into $035F and A.
Entry $9B of group $B1: its square into FB/FC, its byte 3 (pose and hidden bit) = $9C, and the square redrawn.
Never called: A times 4, the high byte in $4D.
How a step in each direction 0-7 moves: 8 east (FB + 1), 4 south (FC + 1), 2 west, 1 north, two of them for a diagonal. North is 0, east 2.

Counts round square FB/FC, for each of the eight directions, the groups other than $033E standing on the next square, into $9700 + direction ($FF for a square off the map), with the straight ones totalled in $9708, the diagonal ones in $9709 and all in $970A; another group on FB/FC itself adds one to each total. FB/FC are kept.
An RTS nothing reaches.

Moves FB/FC a square in direction $033D (step_bits), the start kept (keep_square). A step off the map's edge (past last_column or last_row, or below 0) puts FB/FC back and sets $B0 to 1; $B0 is 0 when the step was made.
Redraws square FB/FC with $033F set, so the cursor (sprite 7) comes over it.
Redraws square FB/FC with $033F clear.
Moves the view a square towards square FB/FC when the square is on the view's edge: left, up, right or down ($B0 = $FF).

Moves entry $9B (group 0) a square in direction $033D: off the map (lift_entry), FB/FC a step (step_square), the view following (follow_view), and back on at the new square (put_entry). Then the cursor over FB/FC when $0342 is set.
Never reached: a JSR to draw_one after move_one's jump.
move_one for $9B of $40 or more, a square rather than an entry: the step and the view only.

One step of a traced line on axis X (0 across, 1 down): the step size ($AC + X) added to the fraction ($C3 + X); when it carries the line moves a square on that axis ($26 + X), back when $28 + X is set.

Sets a line up from $0348/$034A to $0349/$034B: $0353 = $FF, or 0 with $034F = 0 when the ends are one square. Both fractions start at a half ($80); $28 = 1 when the line goes west, $29 = 1 when it goes north. A line straight down steps 0 across and $FF down, one straight across the other way round; any other gets its steps from slope.
The line's lengths: across ($0354) and down ($0355), each without its sign.

The line's ends from entries: for end 1 and then end 0, unless $0344 + end is negative, entry $0344 + end of group $0346 + end gives its square ($0348 + end, $034A + end) and its height (byte 3 less bit 7, into $035C + end).
can_see from entries: the ends (load_ends), then sight.
sight between the squares already in $0348/$034A and $0349/$034B, both at height 0.

Whether end 0 can see end 1, $0353 = 0 when it can. The two heights are worked out (heights) and the line traced from end 0 (line_setup, arc_check, trace) up to $0364 squares: a line of $0364 squares or more, or one that arc_check rules out, cannot see. Along it each square before the end is tested by its figure: a figure no higher (figure_height) than the lower end ($0356) is passed; otherwise the line's height there, rising or falling evenly from end 0's ($0352) by $0350 over the length, must be at least the figure's height, or else the figure's opacity (figure_opacity) is taken from an allowance that starts at $034E; one that leaves the allowance below 0 blocks the line. While both_ways ($0619) is set a clear line is traced again the other way (swap_ends) and must be clear that way too; the ends are swapped back after.

The height of each end: its figure's ground height (figure_ground) plus its own ($035C + end), into $0356 + end. $0352 = end 0's. The lower goes in $0356 and the higher in $0357, $2A = 1 unless end 0 was the lower, and $0350 = the difference.
mark_seen from an entry: the ends (load_ends), then seen_in_view.

For every square of an area 20 across and 10 down from the view's corner (wider than the battlefield's 7 by 7 view), sight from end 0 with end 1's height $036B; each square it can see is redrawn with the cursor (draw_cursor).
line_between: the lists emptied (clear_found), the lengths (distances), the steps (line_setup), then trace.

Traces the line from $0348/$034A: each step (line_step down, then across) gives a square, stored at $9700 (across) and $9780 (down), until the line reaches $0349/$034B or has $0364 squares. $034F = how many, the start not counted. The steps are equal in length (slope), so a square can come twice and the count is close to the line's true length in squares, a diagonal counting about 1.4 a square, rather than the larger of its two lengths.
seen_in_view from square $0348/$034A at height 0.

list_seen: both lists emptied (clear_found, clear_seen); for each entry $0345 of group $0347 that is on the map, sight from entry $0344 (sight_between), and each one it can see goes into $9800 + n (n from 1) with its distance ($034F) at $9880 + n, up to $7F. The count goes in $9800 and the list is sorted by distance (sort_seen).
Sorts the list at $9800 by the distances at $9880, nearest first: passes that swap neighbours out of order, each one shorter than the last, using $034D as the count.

The line's direction as bits: 1 when it runs more across than down, 2 when more down than across, 4 east, 8 west, $10 south, $20 north. $0362 goes up by one when they meet arc_masks' byte for direction $0360.
For each direction 0-7, the bits that rule a line out (line_dirs): direction 2, for one, rules out lines going west or more down than across.

With $0361 not negative, and once only ($FE): a line whose bits meet direction $0360's mask is ruled out ($0362 set). With $0361 not 0, the directions either side are tested too, and the line is ruled out only when all three meet ($0362 = 3); otherwise $0362 = 0 and $0363 = 1. Direction $0360 is left as it was.
Divides $4C/$4D by $AB, $4D below $AB: the quotient in $4B, the remainder in $4D and A.

The steps for a sloping line: the shorter length as 128ths of the longer, rounded ($0366 = 1 when the line runs more down than across), picks the step for the longer axis from step_major and for the shorter from step_minor, into $AC (across) and $AD (down).
slope's RTS, which is also entry 0 of this table, never read. Entries 1 to 128 are the step along a line's longer axis for each slope: 255 x the cosine of its angle, from $FF down to $B5.
step_major's entries 1 to 128, one for each slope.
The step along a line's shorter axis for slopes 0 to 128: 255 x the sine of its angle, from 2 up to $B5. Its first byte is also step_major's entry 128.
step_minor's entries 64 to 128.
Swaps the line's two ends ($0348 with $0349, $034A with $034B), turns $2A over, sets the start height ($0352) to match and turns direction $0360 round (+4).
The view's corner = FB/FC less view_half ($061B), within 0 and last_left/last_top ($0610/$0611); then the view is drawn (redraw_view).
The spare entries' RTSs, eight of them, $CB95-$CB9C.
Fills $9800-$98FF with $FF.

Moves the cursor, sprite 7, over screen square $4E/$4F: 8 x (3 x column - 2) + 24 across and the same with 50 down (sprite_corner), setting the ninth bit of X ($D010 bit 7) when needed but never clearing it; a 7-square view never needs it. A and X are kept.
The sprite position of the screen's top left corner: 24 across, 50 down.
